messages:
maria: Quick sync 1: trace KV store costs are up. We need an eviction/residency model that protects runtime lookups but reclaims analytics churn.
jon: TL;DR on consumer patterns?
maria: Two consumers: (1) runtime online enrichers (latency-sensitive) and (2) batch analytics. Currently everything is pinned; analytics keys are rarely used but steady storage cost.
anya: If we evict keys used for billing attribution we'll cause mis-attribution. Need guardrails for billing keys.
sam: Proposal: classify keys into hot/warm/cold. Use hourly classifier combining hits and a billing-impact score. Hot: long TTL + occasional refresh; cold: short TTL + probabilistic eviction.
lee: Add hysteresis to avoid churn. Eg demotion only after 12h of sustained low activity. Also log every residency change with reason code.
maria: Rollout: dry-run in canary 48h -> 50% traffic 72h -> full. Backfill script to pin keys that billing referenced in last 90d before rollout.
jon: Metrics to watch: eviction_rate_by_tier, miss_latency_p95, attribution_fallback_rate. Alert if attribution_fallback_rate > 0.5% for 15m.
anya: Implementation note: classifier should be deterministic and run as a single-shard job per partition; write residency tag metadata and emit transition events.
sam: Example config snippet we sketched: residencyRules: [ {name: hot, min_hits:100, min_billing_share:0.05, ttl_secs:604800}, {name: warm, min_hits:10, ttl_secs:86400}, {name: cold, ttl_secs:3600} ], hysteresis_secs:43200, sticky_billing_days:7
maria: Ownership: eng-platform owns classifier + backfill tooling; eng-runtime owns client-side fallbacks and guardrails. I'll open RFC addendum for thresholds and rollout checklist.
sre-bot: canary-build: dry-run smoke tests passed 705
lee: SGTM.
